body:
Reply to @mkinney's blocker (point 1) - fixed and pushed (`f5181677`).

**There was no issue for this ask, so I filed one: #727.** Searching the open issues turned up nothing covering "the origin gizmos don't say whose zero they are", and upstream #641 is the lathe grooving/parting blade-corner bug, which is already implemented on main (its own decision doc, `docs/decisions/641-blade-corner.md`, and the `#641` references in `crates/tools/src/orientation.rs`, `crates/app/src/posting_nose.rs`, `lathe_blade_corner.rs`). Merging as written would have auto-closed that.

Everything the review listed is renumbered to #727:

- **Title** -> `feat(ui): viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#727)`
- **`Fixes #727`** and the **`Changelog:`** line's trailing reference
- **Decision file** -> `docs/decisions/727-viewport-gizmo-labels.md` (`git mv`, so the diff is a rename) with its `# Decisions for #727` / `## #727 - ...` headings
- **Code mentions** -> `interact.rs` (5), `law_tests.rs` (4), `axis_note_tests.rs` (1), `setup_chip_tests.rs` (1). I checked `git grep -n 641` across the branch afterwards: the only `#641` left belongs to the lathe blade-corner work, untouched.
- Also `origin/main` merged in (merge commit, no rebase, no force-push) - the branch is `MERGEABLE` / clean.

Two things I deliberately did **not** change, both for want of a permitted mechanism:

- **Branch name** stays `issue/641-viewport-gizmo-labels`. Renaming the head ref of an open PR means a new branch plus a force-push or a fresh PR; the process forbids force-pushes. The PR title, body and closing keyword all say #727, so nothing closes by accident.
- **Commit messages** on the branch still say `(#641)` - rewriting them is an interactive rebase of already-pushed commits.

The `#727` claim comment on the new issue records the mapping too.

**Local results on the renumbered branch**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | builds clean |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests setup_chip_tests law_tests` | 71 passed, 0 failed |

Only comments, one doc rename and two test assertion strings changed, so I ran the touched UI test modules rather than the whole suite.

Re the notes: agreed on the `feat(ui)` minor-cut classification, and on splitting the gizmo code out of `interact.rs` - left out of this PR on purpose, it would bury a two-line behavioral change in a move.

Thanks. The maintainer reviewed this and wants one change before merging: **the gizmo names should be configurable, on or off.** For example, a "Show origin names" toggle in the viewport/view settings (persisted like the other view preferences), defaulting to on. A structural test should cover both states. Push to this branch and it'll be re-checked.

Rework done in `dfc87f09` — the toggle, the persistence, and both-state tests.

- **"Show origin names"** checkbox in the browser pane, under "Show world origin axes"; `State.show_gizmo_names`, default on. The flip is view state like the other toggles — never a command, never on the history — and the choice goes out to disk at once. `interact::overlay_labels` gates only the name rows: the triad lines and the X/Y/Z letters never depend on the switch.
- **One wrinkle on "persisted like the other view preferences":** none of today's view toggles (world axes, projection, display mode) persist across restarts — the only per-user preference file is the recents one. So this adds a sibling `view.json` (`camcraft-view/1`, same config folder, same format discipline, unknown-key tolerant, atomic write): the first persisted view preference gets a home the others can move into later. Say the word if you'd rather it fold into `recent.json` — it's a mechanical move.
- **Tests:** the law test `the_name_switch_quiets_names_not_letters_or_lines` covers both states (names go, letters and lines stay); app `tests/view_prefs.rs` (round-trip, corrupt file starts with names on, unknown keys ride through); egui `tests::view_names` (real checkbox clicks both ways queue nothing, the file follows the click, a restart over the same file keeps the choice); the structural live list gains the checkbox label.
- **Pins:** the new checkbox row moves the painted tree down one row (+21.0 = row height + item spacing), so the hardcoded browser-pane tree tops in `tests.rs` and `tests/program_entry.rs` move `200.0` → `221.0` — the same move `30479ed7` made (`179.0` → `200.0`) for the Projection row. Pixel snapshots untouched (the release lane owns the PNGs, #255).

Gates: ui lib 448 passed / 0 failed (5 GPU ignores), app suite green, `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. (One app test, `fixture_library::the_library_folder_...`, fails on my Windows box but fails the same on clean HEAD — environment, not this change.)

﻿Both re-review asks addressed in 91e36cb9 (main merged in first; CI's gates should re-run on the trial merge):

- Both-states structural check: `structural::origin_names_paint_on_and_quiet_off_letters_and_lines_always` in `structural.rs`. The seeded document's G54 offset sits at world zero and its triad carries the name row, so that is the probe: on, `"G54"` paints inside the viewport (the properties pane also reads G54, so the check anchors between the pane texts, as the view-cube check does); the checkbox click drops it from the painted frame while the X/Y/Z letters and the triad's segments come through untouched. The test redirects `state.view_store` to a temp folder so the at-once persist never writes the real user's view.json.
- `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`: rather than drop the claim, `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs` gained `the_config_dir_override_houses_the_view_file` - fake getter as `recent_files`' resolver test uses, `recent::config_dir_for` must return the override, then a save/load round-trip of a flipped flag under `<override>/view.json`.

PR body and the `Changelog:` line updated to name the "Show origin names" switch and its view.json persistence.

Local gates: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` 490 passed / 5 ignored; `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test view_prefs` 5 passed; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

The owed checked-state assertion is in (`f59031c8`), plus two one-line seam fixes the merge from main dragged in. Head is `0f21a4cd`.

**Request 1:** `origin_names_paint_on_and_quiet_off_letters_and_lines_always` now pins the checkbox's own AccessKit state in both states, sitting right next to the existing `show_gizmo_names` flag asserts:

```rust
assert_eq!(
    h.get_by_label("Show origin names").accesskit_node().toggled(),
    Some(egui::accesskit::Toggled::True), // Toggled::False after the click
    "the checkbox reads checked in the default state"
);
```

One naming note: in this stack (egui 0.36 / kittest 0.4 / accesskit 0.24) the checked state is `node.toggled() -> Option<Toggled>` - accesskit 0.24 renamed `checked` to `Toggled`, and it is nameable in tests as `egui::accesskit::Toggled`. egui sets `True`/`False` from `info.selected` for this checkbox (not `Mixed`), so both states pin cleanly and the test passed on its first run.

**Seam law:** with main merged in, `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam` flags two direct prints on this branch, so both went through the seam, one line each:
- `refusal_ghost.rs:44` - pre-existing on main (the gate is red on clean `origin/main` on its own); picked up as a cherry-pick of the same fix, `1c8583f2`.
- `state_view.rs:23` - this branch's own view loader, added by `dfc87f09`; fixed in `0f21a4cd`.

**Local results at head `0f21a4cd`:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` | 533 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test view_prefs` | 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |

The WORLD_LABEL contrast note: agreed it is low-contrast on the light ground; leaving it out of this PR's scope, it belongs with the light-inks follow-up.

Blocker fixed — the labels are capitalised now (`89cb3d5e`), and I've merged current `main` in since: head is `a912f6ac`, which contains `f490458a`, so the "fails on the merged tree" failure mode from your last review is checked away rather than assumed.

The merge collided on one file: main's #877 added `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs` (theme/colour-vision prefs) where our app::view suite lived. They're separate features writing separate files on disk (`prefs.json`/`camcraft-prefs/1` vs `view.json`/`camcraft-view/1`, separate State fields), so both kept their code and our suite moved to `crates/app/tests/view_file.rs`.

**Tested at the merged head:** the #645 pin set (structural/gizmo/view_names) 23 passed, `--test view_file` 5 passed, main's `--test view_prefs` 6 passed, full ui lib 539 passed / 5 ignored, app lib 110 passed, scoped clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean.

One heads-up unrelated to this PR: `path_lines::tests::the_mark_follows_the_colour_vision_palette_and_the_dim` (the #877 theme test) flakes under repeated local runs on this machine — pristine `main` at `bac4d015` flakes it 5/16 runs, this branch 8/12, same failure both times, so it looks like a pre-existing theme-state race rather than anything this branch introduces. Your CI runs here have stayed green, so it may be load- or ordering-sensitive. Happy to file it as a follow-up issue if useful.
